topic: Dracula's Transylvania was in Hungary, not Romania, when the novel came out (1897)

claims.text: Bram Stoker's Dracula was published in 1897; the Count's castle is in Transylvania.
claims.quote: Dracula is an 1897 Gothic horror novel by Irish author Bram Stoker (drwiki); to stay at the castle of a Transylvanian nobleman, Count Dracula (drwiki); Gothic horror novel published in 1897 (gutenberg); the story follows solicitor Jonathan Harker's terrifying encounter with Count Dracula in Transylvania (gutenberg)

claims.text: From 1867 until 1918 Transylvania was part of the Kingdom of Hungary within Austria-Hungary (the Dual Monarchy), ruled from Budapest.
claims.quote: it was reincorporated into the Kingdom of Hungary ( Transleithania ) as part of the Austro-Hungarian Empire (trwiki); Romanian nationalism smoldered in Transylvania during the period of the Dual Monarchy (cs4); notified the Budapest government that it had assumed control of twenty-three Transylvanian counties (cs5)

claims.text: Stoker never visited Transylvania (no evidence he ever went).
claims.quote: Yet, Stoker never visited Transylvania, much less Bran Castle. (natgeo); there is no evidence that Stoker ever visited either Transylvania or Bran Castle (bran)

claims.text: In the late 1800s the Kingdom of Romania bordered Hungary along the Transylvanian mountain passes; Transylvania and Wallachia are divided by the Carpathian mountains.
claims.quote: left unprotected the Transylvanian mountain passes into Hungary (cs4); guarded the one mountain pass running between Transylvania and Walachia (natgeo)

claims.text: After defeat in World War I, Austria-Hungary broke apart.
claims.quote: Following defeat in World War I , Austria-Hungary disintegrated. (trwiki); Austria-Hungary was disintegrating (cs5)

claims.text: In 1918 (1 December) elected Romanian representatives of Transylvania proclaimed union with Romania at Alba Iulia.
claims.quote: Elected representatives of the ethnic Romanians from Transylvania, Banat, Crișana and Maramureș backed by the mobilization of Romanian troops , proclaimed Union with Romania on 1 December 1918 (trwiki); A mass assembly later that month in Alba Iulia (southern Transylvania), passed a resolution calling for unification of all Romanians in a single state (cs5)

claims.text: The Treaty of Trianon (1920) made Transylvania part of the Kingdom of Romania.
claims.quote: Transylvania became part of the Kingdom of Romania by the Treaty of Trianon in 1920

claims.text: Vlad III, 'Vlad the Impaler' (Vlad Dracula), was the ruler (voivode) of Wallachia.
claims.quote: commonly known as Vlad the Impaler (vlad); was Voivode of Wallachia during three separate r (vlad); Hunyadi installed Vlad Tepes (1456-62) on Walachia's throne (cs8)

claims.text: Bran Castle is marketed as 'Dracula's Castle'; according to a local historian, Romania's communist-era tourism officials picked it in the 1960s because it looked Gothic.
claims.quote: Marketed outside Romania as Dracula's Castle (bran); In the 1960s, when Romania was ruled by a communist government, its tourism czars decided it could be advantageous to market a place associated with Vlad Tepes (natgeo)

claims.text: There is no evidence that Stoker knew anything about Bran Castle; it is not mentioned in the novel.
claims.quote: There is no evidence that Stoker knew anything about this castle; Bran Castle is not mentioned in the novel Dracula

myths.truth: It is not in the novel and there is no evidence Stoker knew of it; it was marketed to tourists from the 1960s.
Vlad III ruled Wallachia, across the Carpathians (he was born in Sighișoara, Transylvania, then in the Kingdom of Hungary).

open_questions: The Library of Congress study places the Alba Iulia assembly 'later that month' after 1 December; Wikipedia gives 1 December 1918. The script says only 'in 1918'.
